utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Examination-in-chief by the Prosecution continuing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Reidy: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, at the close of yesterday's session you had begun to describe a number of beatings that you received whilst you were detained in the gymnasium of the primary school and you had testified to the Chamber that you had been beaten once by Mr. Milan Simic, and it's this incident that I'd like to concentrate on this morning. Could you explain to us the circumstances in which Mr. Milan Simic beat you? Did he himself come to the gym in the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't come with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he himself ever come to visit at the gym in the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know that he had come to visit at the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One evening - I don't know what time it was - we heard some noise and some shouting, and we were ordered to start singing the Chetnik songs. At that moment, in the hall in which we were in, a number of people came in and they started beating us, in order. At one particular moment, somebody started to call out the names of people who were supposed to go out. When I say "out," I mean out into the corridor, towards the changing rooms attached to the gym of the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it -- well, names were being called out. Was your name amongst those ones -- amongst the names?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you went out into the corridor towards the changing room, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They called some others out as well, some other prisoners. My brother Muhamed was among them, Ibrahim Salkic was another, Perica Misic, and others. But that first time they called four or five of us out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So the four or five of you who were called out, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went off towards the changing room, and in the corridor, that is to say, as you come out of the gym, I saw Mr. Simic, and he appeared to me to be slightly tipsy. He seemed to be just about to cry. And then he turned to me and addressed me. He said -- that is, he accused me of my people killing -- having killed his best friend, a roommate of his while they were students. I think his surname was Smiljanic. And I think I knew him too, because he worked in the municipality, the incomes department or somewhere like that, but he was a municipality inspector. When he told me this, I asked him which people. "Which of my people are you referring to?" And he said, "The Muslims." I tried to tell him that I had nothing to do with any of that. And then later on, I heard that Smiljanic had really been killed in an attack on a Croatian village called Kornica [Realtime transcript read in error "Konjic"] or maybe it was Gradacac. I'm not sure, but in that region anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told him that you really had --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There is a problem in the transcript. It says Konjic. The Croatian village of Kornica, not Konjic. Kornica is a town in -- Kornica is K-o-r-n-i-c-a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Kornica. Thank you. Yes. The Prosecution can confirm with the witness whether that is the village he meant, the name, the correct name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, if you can help us clarify the record. The Croatian village you mentioned, can you repeat its name for us, and even perhaps maybe if you could even spell it just to make sure we're absolutely clear on it.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must have been a mistake, because I said and had Kornica in mind and not Konjic. And Kornica is a village which is about 10 kilometres away from our own town and I know it well. So the name I said was Kornica. That was what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After you tried to tell Mr. Simic that you had nothing to do with that, was that the end of the matter? Did he let you then go back into the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know what he did at that particular moment, what he was doing, but when we ended this brief dialogue, they started to beat us in that area where we were in, and I think it was -- it was the passageway towards the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said they began to beat you. Could you tell us, how did they beat you, with kicks or did they use instruments?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They started -- people started beating us who were with Mr Simic. I don't know how many of them there were, but they started beating us with their own weapons, whether rifles or whatever, because it was getting rather dark at this time. I know that we fell down, and when we fell on the floor, they kicked us with their legs so that we had to get up. What can I say? We were beaten a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten -- whereupon your body were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was haphazard. All over, on our heads, all over our bodies. And when we were down, it depended where the kick landed. Usually they aimed at the head, but they weren't fussy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall whether Milan Simic himself personally hit you or did anything else to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular moment, I can't say who beat me. All of them who were there, who had accompanied him, whether they were his bodyguards or escort or whatever. And I heard that they referred to the gentleman as "president." They called him president. I don't know which president, but I knew that they were addressing Mr. Simic. And afterwards, we were ordered, that is to say I was and my brother was, and I think Salkic too, I'm not sure whether they ordered Perica Misic as well, but anyway, they said that we had to get up if we were not already standing and that they should line up in front of Mr. Simic. The escorts ordered us this, to place our hands behind our backs and to stand with our legs apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you -- if you did what they said, what happened after you'd complied with their instructions?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we had to do what they had ordered. And I know that Mr. Simic started hitting me in the area of my genitals. I fell down from each blow. I was ordered to get up immediately and to stand to attention the way I had been so that the president could have a clear target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these blows accompanied by any other threats or any utterances or were they carried out in silence?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the gentleman was saying at that particular moment, but I did hear one of the escorts who issued orders to us and who had beaten us previously, who told us to stand the way we had to stand, anyway, I heard one of them say something along the lines of, "You should target properly so that they can no longer make any balija children." It wasn't Mr. Simic who said that but one of his escorts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Reidy. Mr. Bicic, what did Mr. Simic hit you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic hit me I think only with his leg. He kicked me in the genitals. Or, rather, his boot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said that Mr. Simic kicked you in the genitals. Was he armed at the time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he had an automatic pistol or a Scorpio [sic].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he had an automatic pistol or a Scorpio [sic]? Did you see it with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was standing opposite me, 1 or 2 metres away. I don't know how far away actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any stage did he use his pistol or Scorpio [sic]?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me again. Could you tell us, Mr. Bicic what is a Scorpio [sic]? I'm assuming it's a weapon of some kind, but I haven't heard of the name before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A Scorpion, in fact --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: With an N.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- is a small type of automatic weapon or an automatic pistol. Perhaps that would be a better name for it. You can use it for a burst of gunfire or for individual gunshots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. This Scorpion which you've just described to us, did Mr. Simic ever use it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Simic, at one moment, shot above my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether -- or how Mr. Simic was dressed? Was he in a uniform, in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said he came with a number of either bodyguards or escorts. Were those persons in military uniform or in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were all in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel. Witness, about how many were they, the group that Mr. Simic came with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That time there were at least five or six of them. I can't give you an exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified how you were kicked in the genitals. Do you know whether any of the other people you've mentioned received similar treatment to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that at that particular moment, when they were beating me, my brother and Ibrahim Salkic had to stand there too, and they were beaten in similar fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned Mr. Milan Simic by name. Did you know any of the other people who were escorting him or were acting as his bodyguards?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anybody personally, and I can't remember who those people were now. But quite obviously, they were with him, his escorts, and I heard them address him as "president" on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask the usher to show the witness photographs 64, 57, and 58 from Prosecutor Exhibit 14A, and perhaps you could place number 64 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, if you can see what is now being depicted on the screen in front of you, do you recognise this room or building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us where it is?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the changing room belonging to the gymnasium of the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand it was in and around this changing room that this beating took place, or was it another location?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't in that room. In this room - and I can indicate that for you - the wall is missing which used to be there, and the door too, so that's where that was. This is where the wall was and this is where the door was, and this was the entrance to the changing room. There were metal bars on this window here. And I know the surrounding area very well. This is the basketball playing ground here and the football field was to the left. So they didn't actually beat us in the changing room but in the passageway here, going towards the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I ask whether photograph number 57 could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Bicic, do you recognise the area that's portrayed in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, for the record and for the Chamber, explain to us what is depicted in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depicts the corridor, the entrance to the gymnasium, and this was the door of the gymnasium and that's the hall we were in.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Finally, if you could place photograph number 58 on the ELMO. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I can see it's a door. If you could tell us whether you recognise the door, and if so, what you know about it.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you zoom back a bit? The door doesn't tell me a great deal, but I think it's the entrance from outside, from the courtyard inside, and the corridor of the -- leading to the gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do I understand that, if you're correct, you're saying this is the entrance that links what we saw in the other photographs portrayed from inside the building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with the photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, could you estimate how long you were out in the corridor undergoing this beating?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to say exactly, but I think it went on for about 20 minutes. That would be my approximation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And after this 20 minutes, what happened to you then?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that as far as I was concerned, the peak was reached when this shot was fired above my head, and after that we were ordered to go back to our places. Other people were taken out. What happened to them, I don't know. All I know is that I heard them beating others too; that is to say, I deduced this from the screams and groans. I realised that they were beating other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say other people were taken out. Can you recall now any -- if you remember any of the names or if you know who else might have gone out?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned some names. I think that afterwards they took several, at least several prisoners out, and I think that one of them was most certainly Safet Hadzialijagic, nicknamed Coner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see Mr. Milan Simic on any other occasion whilst you were detained in the gym of the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this before or after the beating you've described to us?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how long after this beating?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately a week later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what took place at this meeting, or did Mr. Simic come into the gymnasium to talk to you, or what happened?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was similar but not so bad. Some people burst into the room where we were. We were ordered to sing, which meant we had to stand up quickly and sing in unison, sing those Chetnik songs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, after you sang the Chetnik songs, did Mr. Simic come into the room or, like the last time, were your names called out?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't come in, but they called out my name and the name of Perica Misic. They called us out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I clarify? Is this Perica Misic the same person who was called out with you when you went to the corridor to be beaten?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was the same person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons who called out your names were -- who were they? Were they guards or people from -- who weren't normally in the prison or in the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who it was who called out Perica Misic's name and mine, whether it was the regular guards - I'm referring to the police that guarded us - or if it was someone from Mr. Simic's escort, but Perica Misic and I went out very quickly. When I say "out," I mean out into the corridor of the gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you went out into the corridor of the gym, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mr Simic again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he address you personally?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he addressed me, but this time he was very polite. By this I mean that he didn't threaten me. I think he was sober. He said he had come for Perica Misic and me and that we were to go for a brief interview in his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you indeed go for a brief interview in his office?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment, he said his car was parked outside the gym and that Perica Misic and I should wait for him next to his car and he would be with us in a moment, and we did what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone try to stop you leaving the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after you went to wait beside the car, could you then tell us -- continue and tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went out and waited for Mr. Simic and his escort. In my estimation, we waited for between five and ten minutes, and then he turned up with the man accompanying him, and he told him to drive in the direction of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you clarify? When you say "the direction of the municipality," is that a location or a building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the building of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go then directly to the building of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go instead?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simic asked me, I can say quite kindly, whether I wished to see my house, and I said yes. Then he told the driver to drive in the direction of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I take it that you went to your house? What happened when you drove up to your house?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Driving toward my house, about a hundred metres away from my house, when we were passing by my catering establishment, we saw from the car Mr. Pisarevic, Mr. Borislav Pisarevic. At that moment, Mr. Simic asked me, probably knowing that I knew Mr. Pisarevic, whether I wished to say hello to him, and I said yes. He told the driver to stop, we got out of the car, and I said hello to Mr. Pisarevic very warmly. And this did not last long. We returned to the car and drove to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us roughly what time of the day was this all taking place at?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was happening at night. In any case, it was after midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you give us some idea of what you would have looked like at this moment? For example, you said yesterday that at one stage you caught a reflection of yourself in the mirror and you were unrecognisable. Was this before or after this outing to your house?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now, I couldn't answer this question with any certainty, but in any case, my clothes and especially my shoes were bloodstained. There was a lot of blood on them. I'm not referring to fresh blood, but the numerous beatings I had gone through before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the blood and bits of skull you described which fell on your clothes when Dikan was being killed, would they still have been -- were they the same clothes you were wearing?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the same clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said after you spoke with Mr. Pisarevic that you then drove to your house. Did you then enter your house or did you just stop outside it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do when you went inside?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simic asked me whether I wished to see the inside of the house, and I said yes. And I asked him, if I managed to find some things that had not been taken away, whether I could change, change my clothes, and he said, "Yes, of course," but I shouldn't stay there too long and that I shouldn't tell anyone that he had allowed me to do this. Then either he or his driver, they gave me a flashlight with which I entered my house. Perica Misic stayed in the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you entered your house, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shocked. The place had been ransacked, looted, smashed up. When I went upstairs, all the doors were open. At one point, I shone the flashlight into my mother's room. She used to have a leather-covered couch in her room, and this had been ripped up, probably by various visitors looking for valuables. I didn't linger there. I went to my room, the room where I kept my clothes. Everything had been thrown about. Nothing was in its place. A lot of things were missing, as far as I could see at first glance. And then I stood there for a short time considering what I should take with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you take with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the end, I only changed my shoes, which were covered with blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you changed your shoes, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to the car, got in, and returned the flashlight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you then proceed to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simic told the driver to drive to the municipal assembly building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that the driver did then drive to the municipal assembly building, and what happened when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simic was very tolerant and kind that evening, and he suggested we should go to his office for an interview. So we went to his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he interview you in the office?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't question us at all. It was rather a friendly chat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that all that happened, you had a friendly chat, or ...

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll describe it briefly. We went into his spacious and beautifully furnished office. It had very nice furniture. We sat down at the table and he told the man escorting him to bring us something to eat and drink. Our conversation was approximately as follows: Addressing both me and Perica Misic, Milan apologised for what had happened seven days ago and told us he had been in a very bad situation, that we should understand him and try to understand what it was like when one lost one's best friend. Of course, at that moment we accepted his apology. And later on, Mr. Simic said to me that there was something else that was important and that he wanted to tell me that evening, and that was that they in the Crisis Staff - he was referring to the Crisis Staff - had decided that my brother and I were to be exchanged. This news made me very happy and gave me hope that we would survive. After that, we had something to eat and drink. I think we drank beer. Milan chatted to Perica Misic, and we stayed there almost until daybreak, in some sort of informal, we might say, friendly conversation. And in the early morning hours, Mr. Simic and his driver or escort took us back to the gym in the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you returned, then, to the gym of the primary school, did you go back into the room where all the other detainees were?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived to the front of the gym in the car. Mr. Simic then suggested to me that, if I wanted, I could take a few cartons of cigarettes from the boot of the car we had arrived in. I can tell you, I wasn't very modest. There were about six cartons, each containing ten packets of cigarettes, in the boot of the car. I looked at Simic and he gave me a look indicating that I could take as much as I wanted, that I could help myself. Since we were very short of cigarettes at the time and cigarettes represented a fortune, I took four cartons, which means there were 40 packs. So when I re-entered the gym, my brother was very worried about me. He was almost crying, because he didn't know where we had been taken, and he had been in great fear until dawn, not knowing where we were and what was happening to us. And when I returned, he cried for joy. This was an understandable reaction, because he had been very worried. He thought something terrible might have happened to us. I told him briefly that everything was all right. I distributed the packets of cigarettes. I gave one to each person, more or less. And I couldn't wait long to tell my brother the most joyful news. From the moment we had been arrested, this was the best news we had had, and that was that Mr. Simic had told me that it had been decided the two of us should be exchanged. I wish to mention that when we were talking in Mr. Simic's office, he discreetly mentioned to me that at the Crisis Staff they had decided that my brother and I should not be exchanged at the same time but that we should be exchanged separately, and I asked him to use his influence and authority to prevent my brother and I from being separated. And he told me he would do his best, but he told me right away that it would be difficult because a definite decision had already been reached at the Crisis Staff. I told my brother all this that morning, and we were both happy and sad at the same time, because there was a possibility that one of us would be exchanged before the other and the other would have to stay behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When Mr. Simic was giving you this information about the exchange, did he ever enlighten you as to his relationship to the Crisis Staff or why on a previous occasion people had been calling him "Mr. President"?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that informal chat in his office, he told us in a discreet way, not as if he was boasting about it, that he was the president of the Executive Council of the Municipal Assembly, and we didn't talk about the Crisis Staff at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm going to take you back now to the primary school, when you had been returned and you've told your brother news about the exchanges. How long more did you remain in the primary school after this evening, or after that evening?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimation, about three weeks passed before I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those three weeks, were you left alone or did the beatings you've described previously continue?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beatings continued as before. Perhaps sometimes they were even worse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would be beating you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the regular beaters, that is, Todorovic and his escort, there were also others who came. There was a certain Rade from Novi Sad who was especially brutal. He maltreated us terribly. Apart from beating us brutally, he maltreated us terribly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How exactly did he maltreat you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, at one point he ordered my brother to beat me, and then he ordered me to beat my brother, and then he ordered our good Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. friend Ibrahim Salkic to beat my brother and then me. And he enjoyed our boxing matches. At first I tried to only pretend that I was beating my brother. I tried to hit him in the head so that only the sound would be bad, but when I did that, I would immediately be hit on the head with a rifle. I would be hit so hard that I would fall down on the floor. And they would say, "Don't try to pretend." Apart from this, this Rade from Novi Sad, I have already said that he was a very cruel man and he was a frequent visitor, he had various methods of torture. On one occasion, he hit me a few times with his rifle butt. He hit me in the head so that I fell down, and then he stood on my chest - he was wearing a military uniform and military boots - and then he jumped up and down all over my body. He jumped up into the air and landed on my chest, my stomach, and my ribs, in his boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sustain any injuries as a result of this beating or other beatings?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the consequences of that beating were that I suffered several injuries, that is to say, on my left-hand side my ribs were broken, fractured. And then with the baseball bat they broke my fingers. The young guy nicknamed Cera - his real name was Nebojsa - had already broken my fingers in the Territorial Defence, but they were injured again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you testified that you were exchanged at the beginning of July. Could you tell us how you came to learn the day that you were to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that up until the very day of the exchange itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the day of the exchange, what happened?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day of the exchange, a man came in. I think he was wearing a police uniform. And he had a list with him, and he started out reading some names from that list. Among those names was my own. My brother's name was not on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the names were called out, what happened? Were you taken out of the room, were you made separate inside the room from the others, or what exactly happened?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point when my name was read out, I did not even have a few seconds to say goodbye to my brother, because the people in uniform began to beat me straight away. They beat me for about ten minutes with their rifles. They kicked me with their legs. They were very brutal. And during those beatings, I felt that they were breaking my ribs all over again. And they just stomped on me. I was lying down and they stomped on me. And my brother had to watch all this. That was by way of a goodbye, a farewell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they had beaten you, did they then remove you from the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the prisoners who were going for the exchange and who hadn't been beaten that badly helped me. They helped take me to the place where they were supposed to go, where they were organising the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand that you had difficulty in walking after the beating?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did the other prisoners help you go to? Was it to the exchange itself, to a bus, to another building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They helped me go to the place where the exchange was to take place. They helped me to the bus which was parked on a plateau between the two halls, that is to say, the gymnasium attached to the primary school and the secondary school centre. I saw three buses there, big ones, and I think there were two kombi vans as well. They were mostly full of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of people? Were they soldiers, civilians?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I boarded one of the buses, I saw that the people there were mostly fairly old people, men and women, and that there were quite a lot of women with children. I didn't see anybody in uniform, of the prisoners or anybody like that going to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where these women and children were from?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew most of them by sight. Some of them were from our town, that is to say, from Bosanski Samac, but most of them were from the surrounding villages. So they were Croats, in fact. They were from the Croatian villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many -- you were one of the people who went to the buses. How many from the primary school actually went on the buses to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure, but I think there were about ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that the -- I think you said three buses and two kombi vans, that they were full of the people from the surrounding villages and only ten prisoners went to join them.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "ten," I meant the people from my group. As to the other prisoners from other places or from other prisons, I can't say. I can't give you an answer to that. I don't know how many of them there were or whether they were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on your bus, is it correct that there were a significant number of elderly people and women and children?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The bus was full. My bus was full, just like the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were getting on the buses, you said there was somebody who had called out your name from a list. Was there anybody else around who seemed to be in charge of the people who were on the buses?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people who were organising the buses and the people?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know some of those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the defendants among them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate which of the defendants were amongst them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing Mr. Tadic, Miroslav Tadic, with some lists of some kind, and I saw them asking him about the exchange and the whole organisation. I think he was in charge of the exchange, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said, "I saw them asking him." Who do you mean when you say "them"?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's just -- you said that you saw them -- "I saw them asking him about the exchange," and my question is: Who was it who was asking Miroslav Tadic about the exchange? Who does the "them" refer to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know who actually asked him something in particular, but everybody seemed to be asking him things, and I saw that he had lists with him, so I assumed that he was in the organisation for this exchange in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you yourself ask him anything?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in a position to at that particular moment. That is to say, my friends had advised me that as I had been so beaten up -- actually, the people who beat me just prior to the exchange, they kept swearing at that policeman, cursing him, who read my name out of the list for the exchange. They told him that there was absolutely no chance that I would be exchanged alive, that I would still be living. They -- I think they said this to him while they were beating me just before the actual exchange. So that they advised me that as soon as my name was read out from the list, I was to board the bus and to try and find a seat somewhere where I wouldn't be seen from outside. I myself felt the need to sort of hide, kept a low profile, because I was afraid that Todorovic might turn up, or someone like him, who, quite simply, could forbid me to go for the exchange. Because those old people, the women and the children who were there made room for me in the back part of the bus, and I stayed there until the actual exchange took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did the buses take you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started out first towards Brcko and then Bijeljina and then on towards Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually cross the border into Serbia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did cross the border and we entered Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then -- were you then exchanged in Serbia or did you again leave Serbia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They drove us to a place called Sid, which is near the Serbian-Croatian border. There was a motel which was called the Motel Sid, taking its name from the town, and that is on the Belgrade-Zagreb motorway, not many kilometres away from the demarcation line, or rather, at that time it was the place where UNPROFOR was stationed. I think that UNPROFOR took part in our exchange. Anyway, we were brought to Sid on that first lap, to the Sid Motel, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then get off the buses and stay in the Sid Motel?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not get off the bus. Let me just say that on the road to Sid, we were stopped frequently at checkpoints by the military or whoever was manning the checkpoints and wearing uniform. Sometimes they would board our bus and threaten to cut our throats, said that they would kill us and that we shouldn't be allowed to go free. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meantime, one of the buses broke down, so we all had to wait for the bus to be repaired, so that we arrived in Sid in the late afternoon. Perhaps it was evening already. So that the exchange was not organised that day. It did not succeed in taking place that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do for the evening, then?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening we spent in the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is all the women and the children. Was there a toilet on the bus? Had you received food during your arduous journey to Sid?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the journey to Sid we were not given any food and we couldn't relieve ourselves, we couldn't get off the buses, so that some of the children and the elderly women had to urinate in the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you said that you spent the evening in the buses, and then can you take us to the next morning and tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night was a particularly difficult night for us, because we were afraid that the exchange would never actually take place. I don't think any of us slept at all. I saw the old women and old men who had been collected up from the Croatian villages were praying to God, praying that everything should go well and that they could get out of the situation and go to Croatia. In the morning, at daybreak, they brought us some food, and I can say that compared to what I had experienced before that, that the food was plentiful. I think that that too was organised by Mr. Tadic, the food and everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So after you'd had some food, did you then remain in Sid [Realtime transcript read in error "SIT"] or did you move on to a different location to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed at the motel or, rather, in front of the motel where we were parked and where we had spent the night. And after breakfast or after having something to eat in the early morning hours, I asked to be allowed to meet with Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just continue. For the transcript, I think it's a problem with my pronunciation of B/C/S. Line 20 of page 24 has -- my question says: "Did you remain in SIT?" and I meant Sid, which I understand is spelled S-i-d, and just -- because SIT is also the name of the factory in Bosanski Samac, and I wouldn't like there to be any confusion for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So my question referred to Sid. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Bicic, just a technical problem. Can I take you back to your last testimony, which was that you asked to be allowed to meet Mr. Tadic. Was your request granted?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask anybody. I had no reason to ask somebody to be allowed to talk to him because we weren't tied there or anything else. We were allowed to eat and step down from the bus. But I had been rather busy, and I tried to seize an opportunity to speak to him, which I succeeded in doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you want to speak to him about?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I asked him whether he could spare a few minutes for me, and he said yes. And I wanted to talk to him about my brother, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it about your brother that you wanted to raise with him? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I knew that Mr. Tadic knew me very well, I thought I had every right to ask him, in very -- to ask him to use his authority to ensure that my brother would be exchanged as quickly as possible. I humbly requested him to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his response?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that he would do his best. I thanked him in advance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After this -- when you actually got an opportunity to speak with Mr. Tadic, was this still in Sid or was it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was still in Sid, before noon, while we were waiting and while we were still not sure whether the exchange would go through, whether it would actually take place and be successful. So we were still in this state of expectation and incertitude, because there was always the possibility that we might be taken back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in fact exchanged on that day?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, luckily. Sometime between 11.00 and 12.00, we were told that the exchange could start, and we were exchanged that day finally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly did that exchange take place?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exchange took place at a place called Lipovac, I think, which is at the very border between Serbia and Croatia. It is on the motorway running from Belgrade to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I take it that when you were exchanged, you went to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the exchange, I was in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bicic, it's very evident from all the testimony that you've given that you were delighted to be exchanged. Was that because you were delighted to be leaving Bosanski Samac or was it because you were delighted to be released from your detention?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, I think that I had mixed feelings. As happy as I was to know that I would be seeing my mother and daughter again and my sister-in-law and my brother's child, daughter, and that I was finally free, on the other hand, I was very, very sad because I knew the circumstances in which my brother had remained where he was, so that these were mixed feelings. But nevertheless, the I was very happy, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1992, just before your detention, did you have any intention of leaving Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any intention of leaving Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that you left Bosanski Samac of your own free will, that it was your choice to leave Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to that is the following: From the very time of my arrest, nothing was according to my own free will after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask a -- this is to take you back whilst you were in detention. It was a matter you raised yesterday. You said during your detention period that you'd heard rumours that the ICRC were looking for you. Did you ever get a visit by the ICRC in any of the locations in which you were detained?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody of those international institutions, the Red Cross or whatever organisations for assistance or contact with our families or something like that, nobody never came to visit us. And when I say "us," I mean the group of people who were incarcerated with me up until my exchange. Afterwards, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those people who you said yesterday were represented to the ICRC, do I take it they were then first shown to the ICRC and then following their presentation they were incarcerated with you or came to join you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least some of them. I don't know how many were shown to the Red Cross, but I do know that they put some of them in with us, into our group. And it was precisely from one of them that we heard - and I gave you his name yesterday, I think - that I heard why he was there and what had happened to him linked to the visit by the Red Cross and what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll take you back now to your exchange. Can you just tell us, after you were exchanged, you went to Croatia. Did you visit a doctor? Did you require medical attention? What was your physical state of being like, your health?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing that I wanted to do was to try to get rid of my beard, because I had a big beard when I was exchanged, and I never wore a beard in my life. I didn't want my daughter to see me looking like that. And I wanted to change my bloody clothing. I changed my clothes with the help of one of my friends who had received information that I was up for the exchange that day, and he was waiting for me with a fresh change of clothing. And I wasn't able to do away with my beard that first day, so I postponed my meeting with my daughter for the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, it's 11.00. We shall rise and continue our proceedings at 1130 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, at the beginning of your testimony you said that you were currently living in Germany. Have you been back to Bosanski Samac since you were exchanged in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went back, did you visit your old house, properties that you owned?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of -- what did you see when you went to visit them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To start with, my house, my house is ruined. When I say that, I mean that everything that could have been destroyed has been destroyed. Part of the roof is missing. There are no windows, no doors. Some walls have been pulled down. I have even noticed that the plumbing has been removed from the bathroom, that the electricity cables have been taken away. Quite simply, it is a ruin. Of the three catering establishments we had in our town -- or rather, they were not all catering establishments. One of them was a shop selling clothing, and this has also been ruined. Everything has been looted, as was the case with my house. Another business premise that was owned by my brother in the centre, its purpose has been changed. Everything has been looted. My brother actually had a shop there selling games. I'm referring to computer games and snooker and things like that. Everything was looted, and one of the local Serbs, or Serbs who moved in, has a cafe there now. Only the pizzeria was still working, but when it was possible to go there and I visited it, it was in a very bad condition. I heard, however, that it operated throughout this time. It changed owners several times, but it was also thoroughly looted. I think that of everything that was in it, and I can say that it was very well equipped, I managed to see only the oven for baking pizzas, which was so big and so heavy that probably for this reason it stayed behind and was not taken away because they were unable to carry it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the pizzeria changed owners several times, but you were the owner of that pizzeria, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the owner, yes, but by some kind of decree or whatever, all our property was confiscated. And I say it was confiscated because later on, I wrote various requests and applications asking for the restoration of our property, which in the meantime has been looted and ruined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your property was originally confiscated, did you ever receive any payment or consideration in exchange for your property?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I never received any payment or compensation. None of us did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you -- were your applications to have your property restored to you successful?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what would we mean by successful? My opinion, it's impossible to restore something that was looted and damaged for years, so that of all this property, only the pizzeria is still operating. And I hope that after my testimony, it will not be destroyed further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the pizzeria now back in your name, your ownership?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am again the owner of this property. In the meantime, I found a compromise, so I have rented it out to a young man from our municipality whom I knew before the war, and I am satisfied with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the house back in your name or your family's name, whichever?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the ruins of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before the break, you had testified that you had changed your clothes and you were planning to visit your daughter, I believe, in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we leave the change of his positions, Witness, did you have any motor vehicles before you were arrested, and if so, what has happened to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment of my arrest, I had a car - it was a Mercedes - and a jeep. My brother had a car, a Honda. When we evacuated our family before the town was taken over, fortunately we left two cars in Croatia, so that only my jeep was confiscated.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, just talking about properties and the motor cars, for completion, was there anything -- any other property or possessions that you had prior to the war which were confiscated?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have some property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- what was that if it was different from any of the businesses you've talked about, your house, or the cars?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besides catering and my pizzeria, I had another business. I had many gaming machines, football, soccer, billiards, various electronic games, poker machines, about 150 or 160 of these machines. All this has been stolen. I had these on the territory of the municipality of Samac, in the town itself, in Modrica, and in some surrounding villages. I had rented these out, and later on I was not able to get any of it back. It has all been looted or destroyed. That's as far as my property is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. For the jeep you've talked about, and these machines, have you ever received compensation?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Reidy. I wonder, Mr. Bicic, could you tell us how you regained control of the pizzeria? Because from my understanding, there were other persons who were running it in your absence and so on. So I'm just wondering, did you have to pay anything to get control of it again or -- essentially, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, I had to go through paperwork. I had to fill in applications for the restoration of property, and then -- I think they call it the Ministry for the Return of Displaced Persons and Property, and through them I contacted the man who was running the pizzeria at that time. I think his last name was Lazendic. He tried to extort some money or to get some money from me in order to give up my property, but I did not agree to this, and he then told me that he had had to pay the people who had held the place before him. And then he asked me who would give him this money back. I don't know for how many years he had been running the pizzeria. Perhaps four or five. And I told him that I had no intention of paying anything for my own property. And he said that in that case, he would have to take all the things, because he considered them to be his because, as he alleged, he had bought them. We then came to the conclusion, through the mediation of some people from the ministry, that an inventory should be taken of what in the pizzeria was mine, so that when he left it, he would not take away something that was mine. And as I have already told you, all that was left to me was the pizza oven. In the end, when I did not agree to pay for anything, he said to me that he had had to pay for the central heating radiators extra, and he said if I didn't want him to take them away, I should give him 400 German marks. And I replied to him as I had before, that he would not get one German mark from me because I refused to be blackmailed any longer, and I said he was welcome to the radiators. Then I bought new radiators in Germany, the best I could find, and I sent them down there to the young man who rented the place from me and decorated it, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, can I just ask: Mr. Lazendic, who you eventually got your property back from, do you happen to know anything about his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what ethnicity he was? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the owners before him, I mean the several owners you said there might have been, do you know what ethnicity they were?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I just -- yes. What year was this when you finally got your pizzeria back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was about a year and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned a number of businesses and that now you are receiving some rent for your pizzeria. Did you also receive rent from your pizzeria prior to the war or from some of the other business interests you had?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- we ran these business interests. We were the owners. We ran two of them. And the shop my brother had, the shop selling games in the town centre, was one that we rented, and we had an option to buy it, and we invested money in it, so that before the war we did not rent out our property or our business interests at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just ask you to explain one other matter. You said that the situation you've now reached was a compromise, and I just wonder what you mean it's a comprise now that you have someone else running it.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think your explanation on the record was that you've reached a compromise and that a young man is now renting it from you, and I just wanted to know what you meant when you said that this was a compromise.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said it was a compromise, I meant that in all this, I am at least partly satisfied, if one can talk of satisfaction at all in this situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I will now take you back again just to the time of your exchange, and I'd just like you to explain what you did immediately after your exchange. You've told us that you changed your clothes and you planned to meet your daughter. I had asked you whether or not you had at some stage sought some medical attention.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did seek some medical attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the nature of that medical attention?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some good friends of mine from Croatia, from Slavonski Brod, helped me at once to get some medical check-ups with very good doctors in the hospital in Slavonski Brod. After this, most of them said I should be hospitalised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you hospitalised?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just explain to us some of the injuries you had which caused the doctors to suggest hospitalisation?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were various injuries. Most of my internal organs were damaged, my kidneys, my spleen. My fingers were still broken, so were my ribs. But I didn't want to stay in hospital, because I thought if I stayed in hospital, I would not be able to help, to help my brother be exchanged. I was given various medicines, and I used quite a lot of these medicines. However, I did not feel physical pain. The psychological pain was far stronger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would you guess that it took you to recover from the physical injuries and then, secondly, from the psychological pain you've described?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I managed to recover from my physical injuries relatively quickly. And when I say "relatively quickly," I mean after about six months. But as for my psychological suffering, I think I have not recovered yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, the Prosecution has now finished their examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Cross-examination. I would like to know how many Defence counsel will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: One here. And how many on the back? Two. Three in total, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: About three, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. Four? Four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And Mr. Pantelic. Okay. All counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I almost left out Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. And you will start. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Baen:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, my name is Catharine Baen, and I'm one of the lawyers appointed by this Tribunal to represent Mr. Milan Simic, and I'm going to be asking you a few questions mainly just to clarify your earlier testimony. Most of my questions will be phrased where you can answer or where the question calls for a yes or no response. If you don't understand my question, please let me know, and I'll do my best to rephrase it for you. Do you understand everything so far?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I want to talk to you about your relationship with Milan Simic before all the hostilities started taking place in April of 1992. You've testified previously that you knew Milan Simic or you've known him for a long time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you went to primary school together; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your brother Muhamed also has known Mr. Simic for a while; however, did he not go to primary school with Mr. Simic, did he?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was older.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've had an occasion to know Mr. Simic for a longer period of time or more closely than your brother Muhamed; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all events, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your pizzeria, you mentioned in your earlier testimony last week that Milan Simic was a frequent visitor to your pizzeria; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "frequent," you mean maybe three or four times a week?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how many years did Milan Simic visit your pizzeria for three to four times a week?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say for how many years, but of late, let's say a year or six months prior to the war, he was a frequent visitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he came into your pizzeria, he was very friendly with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never had any problems or ugliness with him, did you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no reason. He was always very proper in his conduct as a customer, just as the staff were proper in their conduct towards all the other customers and to him as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he came in there with his wife sometimes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't know his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his father or his parents?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew his father, not his mother, but I did also know his sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they're a nice family, aren't they? Wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends which angle of vision you take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You know from your years, I guess, of knowing Milan Simic, you know that he's an educated man. He went off to the university to study economics. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he studied economics, I did not know, or where or anything of that kind, but afterwards, I assumed so because he worked as an economist or one of the directors, I think, of the timber industry or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Back to the pizzeria for just a moment. You mentioned last Friday that the other defendants in this case did not frequent your restaurant or your pizzeria that much; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't really -- so you didn't see on these three or four occasions -- three or four times a week that Milan came into your restaurant, you did not see him continuously or frequently hanging out or gathering with these other defendants, did you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention who was hanging out with whom, so I can't affirm or deny.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But they didn't come in there that often, and Milan did; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've already asked me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go ahead and answer, and we'll move on. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already answered your question, and my answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, answer this, then: These defendants never had any meetings, political meetings or functions in your restaurant, did they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to ask them that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw them, you were never aware of them having meetings in your restaurant?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my restaurant was not a hall or a place where meetings of that kind would take place, political meetings or functions. That was not its purpose. But if somebody socialised and talked, had discussions, I don't know who that could have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- I'll move away from this topic. I just want to generally ask you, though: Prior to the hostilities, you had no bad feelings towards Milan Simic and, as far as you know, he had no bad feelings towards you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my part, I did not, and I don't think he had any reason to either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to hear when Mr. Simic voluntarily surrendered himself? Did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember where you were when you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I told you that he voluntarily surrendered the end of February 1998, would that sound to be correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the date. I don't know when I heard about it, the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor for the Tribunal in early March 1998. Did they contact you or did you volunteer to give a statement to them when they may have been talking to other witnesses you knew?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they had contacted my brother first, and at that time I think I was in Croatia, so that it was through my brother that I came into contact with the Tribunal, and I said that I would be happy to respond to the Tribunal's invitation to testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was an invitation to your brother and then you volunteered to testify, or the OTP asked you or extended an invitation to you? I'm not quite clear. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clarify that question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. My question is -- this is the way I understand it, and you can tell me if this is correct: The Office of the Prosecutor contacted your brother, Muhamed, to give a statement. At that point, or after that point, you gave a statement at some time in March of 1998. Did you volunteer, did you go to the Prosecutors and say, "Hey, I can give a statement," or did they come to you and say they would like to take your statement?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told my brother that when he was in a position and when he was in contact with the Tribunal, that I would be happy to make a statement myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So apparently he conveyed that to the OTP and then they contacted you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move on to talk to you about your relationship with some of the other people you've testified about today and also who are mentioned in the Prosecution's indictment. First of all, your brother, Muhamed, you've mentioned that he is your older brother. Are you living together now in Germany? I'm not asking where, just: Are you living together?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we're not living together. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When is the last time you did live together?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the same house or the same town or the same country? Could you be more specific when you say "living together"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. In the same town is a good place to start. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time we lived in Bosanski Samac, and then afterwards, after leaving the camp, we would sometimes be together, I mean in the same town, first of all in Croatia, then for a time in Germany, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you gave the statement to the OTP in March of 1998, were you living together in the same town?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when he contacted you about giving his statement, he called you on the phone, or did you go to give your statements together?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether the first mention of the Tribunal came by phone, whether it was over the phone or whether it was when I went to that town to visit our mother. She lives in that town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What town -- to what town are you referring?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the town in Germany where my brother and mother live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's where you were when you gave the statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there at that particular moment, because somebody had paid a visit to my brother, and then I too gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me make sure I understand. You were in Germany, the OTP came and interviewed you there, your brother was there and interviewed in the same place in Germany. Was there anybody else from Bosanski Samac who was interviewed by the OTP there in the same town in Germany when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Ibrahim Salkic was not there and Perica Misic was not there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, I guess, have been here in The Hague for a while waiting to testify before the Trial Chamber. How long have you been here?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been here for a couple of days already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple of days. You were here last Friday to testify. You weren't here prior to your testimony starting on Friday?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a couple of days before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple of days before last Friday. So have you been here about a week now?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your brother came here with you, did he not? You travelled here together?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We arrived together in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time did you and your brother discuss the facts of this case or your testimony here before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
