utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier that people are arming themselves both legally and illegally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also stated that you and your brother Muhamed both bought a couple of illegal weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me what's correct. You bought two weapons for you and your brother. That's not correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is correct is that I purchased the weapons, not my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You purchased them, but you purchased them for your use and your brother's use; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are automatic rifles; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know much about weapons?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it that way. I don't know much about them, but I do know a little bit about them. I know the difference between a pistol and a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a Kalashnikov is?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I procured two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know what it is. That's what you bought; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what an AK47 is?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You purchased these two Kalashnikovs, but prior to your purchase of those two automatic rifles, you and your brother owned together two pistols and a hunting rifle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the weapons we had on paper legally. My brother was a hunter, so he had a hunting rifle, and both of us possessed pistols with licences issued by MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of hunting rifle does your brother own? I'm talking about the legal one that was owned previously.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a normal hunting rifle, but who the manufacturer was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what kind of pistols were these two pistols that you had, the legal pistols?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said in the statement. It was CZ-99.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I see that you did answer that. I'm sorry for that repetition. Having the pistol and the rifle, you still found it necessary to buy these two Kalashnikovs. So you bought these guns, or you went to Odzak to buy those guns; is that correct? Or two guys from Odzak. Excuse me. You brought them from two guys at Odzak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the surrounding parts of Odzak. That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you know -- and you're probably going to think this is a stupid question, but humour me and answer this if you can. Since you said they're illegal weapons, obviously you know that it's against the law to carry those two rifles, those two Kalashnikovs that you bought?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit that the question is a funny one. And secondly, I'm going to answer by telling you that everybody had -- it was legal when the army distributed the weapons, and it was considered illegal if somebody procured these weapons as they were best able to protect their homes. That really is a humourous -- stupid question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Humourous question." Sorry. Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guys -- excuse me. The gentlemen you bought these guns from, their names were Marko and Simo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that it was a man -- a young guy by the name of Simo, but I don't remember a Marko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you paid 1.400 Deutschemarks for these two weapons?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the penalty, do you know, or did you know at the time what the penalty was for carrying illegal weapons like this in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the penalty was severe, perhaps even execution, or at least detention in camps, or something similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've never ever been convicted of a weapons charge?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was convicted to a camp. I assume that that was punishment for the weapons. Or perhaps there's something I don't know about, why I was convicted to the camp and expulsion from the place I was born in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bicic, I'm not -- I'm really not attacking you. I'm just asking questions that are just the general, typical questions that we ask in cases such as this. I asked you had you ever been convicted of a weapons charge, and I'm talking about prior to April 17, 1992.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Convicted by whom? Accused by whom, the Serbian police or what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about in a court of law in the former Yugoslavia. Were you ever convicted? Did you go to court? Were you charged and then convicted of carrying an illegal weapon? I think the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was convicted, as far as I remember at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying you were charged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been convicted of any serious offence? I'm not talking about during the war what happened; I'm talking about prior to April 1992. Were you ever convicted of a criminal offence in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving back to the weapons. You and your brother were not the only ones who obtained illegal weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were other people, Croats and Muslims, who obtained illegal Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. weapons. I think you've already testified that everybody was getting illegal weapons from everywhere; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm wondering why there's so much repetition.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll try to move along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you expect an answer from me or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I can only ask this question one more time or I may get thrown out of here because I'm repeating stuff. I'm sorry to keep repeating. I just want to make sure it's clear for the record. To your knowledge, were there Croatians and Muslims who also obtained -- other Muslims who also obtained illegal weapons? That's all.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first have to answer by saying that there were two angles from which you could view this, whether -- to determine whether weapons were procured legally or illegally, depending on your point of view. From the Serb position, we who procured weapons for the defence of our own lives and homes and families were considered to have procured them illegally, whereas they, the ones who had all these weapons without having to purchase them on the black market or goodness knows which markets, tanks and guns and everything else that goes with them, do you mean to tell me that that was legal, whereas what we did illegal?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just -- I'm going to try to really move this along. Since there were all these illegal weapons being procured from people, all kinds of people, is it possible that members of the SDA had illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, everything was possible when it came to weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did any members of the SDA have illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that people who were in detention with you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I have to object to this line of questioning in the sense that it's purely speculation. Anything is possible. And again Ms. Baen keeps putting questions, "Is it possible that, is it possible that." Simply ask the witness, "Do you know whether anyone detained with you," before it repeats, otherwise it's purely speculation and --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll happily rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because this is a fact witness, so do rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand the Rules, and I messed up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, do you know if any of the people who were in detention with you had been carrying illegal weapons before they had been taken into custody; yes, no, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move away from the weapons. I'd like to talk to you now about some of the other things, illegal things that were happening in the area of Bosanski Samac. Mr. Bicic, you know that there were barricades that were put up in Bosanski Samac during this time of the hostilities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about some and I had to pass through others. When I said "had to pass through," I meant checkpoint. Yes, I had heard that there were some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some of these barricades had been put up by some of these Muslim individuals; is that correct? Is that what you heard?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard something about that, but I personally didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. What I'm asking you is if you heard that some Muslims, the Muslim people, put up the barricades; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I heard about it. I heard that somebody had erected barricades. Now, who ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whoever was putting these up, this is illegal activity, is it not?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any of the people -- or did you hear that any of the people responsible for putting up these barricades ended up in detention in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, you had mentioned, I believe it was on Friday of last week, that at one point you left town to go to Crkvina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I went to Modrica, but I had to pass through Crkvina, or I went via Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you make this trip to Modrica? Was it the week before April 17th?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before the 17th of April, but exactly when, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe just a few days before, possibly?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think it was more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible it could have been around the 13th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I would object again. Is it possible? The witness was on that Friday asked when this occurred, and I believe he's given his answer. I think he refers to it a number of weeks before the 17th of April, and now Ms. Baen, I think, is trying to suggest to him it was another date and asking him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If he doesn't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: -- he doesn't know. Your Honour, if he doesn't know, he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, so --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever leave Bosanski Samac on any other occasion the week of April 17th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I frequently left, in all directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for what purpose were you leaving Bosanski Samac frequently the week of April 17th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly for business reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of business?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was business which I had in connection with the machines that I was renting out in Modrica and Gradacac and Orasje --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of machines was that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and across the border in Croatia. I am referring to billiards, poker machines, video games, football machines, slot machines, and amusement machines.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Not slot machines, but just entertainment or amusement machines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times do you think you left Bosanski Samac that week? Was it each and every day? Was it twice a day? Just some sort of general idea on how many times you left.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varied, depending on the need, how many times I had to go. Sometimes it was once, sometimes twice, and I allow for the possibility of more times in different directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't remember if you left town on April 13th, 1992 specifically, do you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this point in time, I can't remember how many times and where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer is you don't know, you don't remember if you left or not; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you answer me, nine and a half years ago, on such-and-such a date, where you were going and how many times?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I couldn't tell you nine years ago what I was doing on a certain date. I'm just trying to get a general idea about what you were doing the week before April 17th, because it was a very -- I'm putting words in your mouth, but I would think it was a very, very memorable week because of the psychosis of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen, it's 1700 hours by our Court clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How long do you think you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Not very long. I hope I'll go faster tomorrow. I think half an hour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You had the whole of this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I think in half an hour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You had -- we started before lunch hour and you've had the whole of this afternoon. And do you remember that your colleagues also wish to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. I don't think they have very much, and I really don't have that much left. I think it's probably going to be about 30 minutes, seriously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Another half hour?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It's not -- or maybe less. It's not a Mr. Pantelic 30 minutes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It's more of a realistic 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Tomorrow we are not sitting. We shall sit on Thursday and Friday morning and afternoon, and Monday we shall not sit because the courtroom will be used by another Trial Chamber. So Thursday, Friday, and then we proceed -- we continue on Tuesday, morning and afternoon sessions. The Court will adjourn.
